title: Past-Paper Analysis
intro: Built from the official test patterns of PPSC and FPSC and from 180 engineering questions in recent PPSC Assistant Engineer (Civil) 2025 and SDO/AD (Civil) 2018–to-date papers, as recalled by candidates and published on TestPoint. Use it to decide what to revise first. It is a sample, not a full official paper set, so treat the percentages as a guide.

b: ≈ 80% qualification-related (civil engineering) + 20% general ability (GK, Pakistan Studies, current affairs, Islamic studies, English, maths, computer)
FPSC — AEE Civil (Pak PWD, MES and others)
MCQ screening test followed by interview
Mostly professional; check the advert for the exact split
Professional + general ability; often heavier on hydraulics and irrigation for water posts

FPSC professional syllabus (AEE Civil, Pak PWD): Building materials & construction; surveying & levelling; hydraulics & hydrology; concrete technology & RCC design; construction management; structural design applications; sewerage and sewage treatment; engineering materials; ground improvement; CAD; project management.

FPSC professional syllabus (AEE B&R, MES — civil stream): Also adds soil mechanics & foundations, sewage treatment, PC-I for building and infrastructure projects, project supervision, contract management, costing & estimation, water resources & water supply design, steel structures, environmental engineering and basic IT.
💡 Exam point: Every pattern gives about 80 marks to engineering. Your handbooks cover the professional part; general ability needs separate preparation.
180 engineering questions were classified by subject (general-ability questions removed).
Building & engineering materials (cement, concrete, bricks, timber, stone, steel, paints, glass)
Building construction (masonry, arches, doors, roofs, DPC, plaster, formwork, finishes)
Mechanics / strength of materials (stress, strain, elasticity, indeterminacy, stability)
Geotechnical (Atterberg limits, compaction, classification, bearing capacity, earth pressure)
Quantity surveying & project management (estimates, CPM/PERT, contracts, units)
Transportation (road terms, signs, drainage, railways, harbours)
RCC & structural design (steel limits, cover, footings, bar spacing)
Environmental / public health (water supply, sewerage, air limits, solid waste)
💡 Exam point: Materials + building construction ≈ 40% of the engineering marks. Revise those two handbooks first and best.

Department effect: Papers for Irrigation, WASA/PHE and C&W posts lean towards their own field: expect more irrigation & hydraulics in Irrigation/WAPDA papers, more water supply & sewerage in PHE/WASA papers, and more roads in C&W/NHA papers. Give your department's subject the next-highest priority after materials and construction.
name of a brick part, an arch part, a roof shape, a construction process, a soil limit
minimum steel in a column, height of slump cone, cement-bag volume, bricks per m³, curing days
strain from elongation, reduced bearing from WCB, area of a circle, unit conversion
💡 Exam point: Most marks come from knowing terms and numbers, not from long numericals. The "Numbers to Memorise", "MCQ Traps" and glossary sections pay off most.

Cement: Silica % in OPC; compound responsible for initial set (C₃A); low-heat cement (less C₃A and C₃S); cement with low or high C₃S; cement for sea water / coastal works (sulphate-resisting); free lime and unsoundness.
Concrete: Slump-cone height (300 mm); batching; bleeding; creep; tensile ≈ 10–15% of compressive strength; unit weight of PCC (≈ 2400 kg/m³); which mix ratio is strongest; poker (immersion) vibrator.

Other materials: Softwood from conifers; tree age by annual rings; slaking of quicklime; kaolinisation of feldspar; silica in igneous rocks; uses of blasted stone; oil paint constituents and drying oil (linseed); glass melting point and photochromic glass; stainless steel (chromium); Bessemer process; perlite; gypsum calcination.

Masonry & construction: Frog of a brick; strongest bond (English); voussoirs, intrados, extrados of an arch; cavity wall against dampness; coping; baluster; door sill; hipped roof; eaves; lath; parge coat; dewatering; formwork for ornamental finish; membrane roofs and suspended ceilings.

Estimating & management: Bricks per m³; plaster thickness; cement-bag volume (0.035 m³); hook length (9d); units of measurement; revised estimate when the sanctioned estimate is exceeded by more than 5%; PC-I; liquidated damages; CPM critical event; dummy activity; bar chart = Gantt chart; PERT is event-oriented.

Mechanics: Hooke's law; strain from elongation; factor of safety; statically indeterminate structures; point of contraflexure; stiffness, strength, stability, toughness definitions; Poisson's ratio (highest for rubber); moment of inertia.

RCC: Minimum and maximum steel in beams and columns; minimum number of bars in rectangular (4) and circular (6) columns; maximum spacing of slab bars; bent-up bars resist shear; minimum cover; trapezoidal combined and strap footings; side-face reinforcement.
Soils: Shrinkage limit; groove of Casagrande tool; Proctor mould; AASHTO groups; rapid moisture method; drainage of fine soils (electro-osmosis); Terzaghi bearing capacity; Rankine Ka.

Roads & transport: Regulatory vs warning vs informatory signs; camber; ruts; catch-water and side drains in hill roads; breast and retaining walls; service roads; rail sleepers; berths and breakwaters; mass-transit benefits.

Water & sanitation: Depth of water mains; gate (sluice) valve; aeration removes gases and taste; acidity from CO₂; incinerator; inverted siphon; minimum house-drain gradient; detention time in settling tanks; NO₂ limit in residential air.

Hydraulics & irrigation: Pitot tube; velocity is maximum at pipe centre; lift is normal to flow; Newton's law of viscosity; centrifugal pumps for low head; surge tanks against water hammer; duty; glacis falls; pH of irrigation water.
